key_insight: GA-AMNO separates adaptive meshing into two explicit questions—where to compute and how representations should interact—using physics-informed allocation plus geometry-conditioned Gauge transport to make adaptive neural operators more interpretable and robust.
engineering_relevance: This gives PDE solvers a practical way to improve accuracy under nonuniform, changing meshes while preserving representation compatibility across discretizations, which is important for simulation-driven engineering workflows.
method: Physics-informed adaptive mesh allocation chooses sample locations based on local physical structure.
Gauge-aware low-rank transport maps source features into the target node’s geometric context before aggregation.
Operator-readability enables controlled interventions to inspect and test allocation vs. interaction effects.
evidence_signal: The paper reports experiments on five PDE benchmarks, showing improved predictive accuracy and stronger cross-discretization compatibility under geometric mismatch.
watch_item: The transport step adds modeling and implementation complexity, and performance may depend on the quality of geometric conditioning and on meshes that preserve topology.
paper_title: Where to Compute and How to Interact: Operator-Readable Adaptation with Gauge-Aware Transport
